The FOMC’s June 2017 statement points to moderate growth, continued labor-market strengthening, and inflation running somewhat below 2%, alongside a 25 bp rate hike and guidance that the funds rate will remain below its longer-run level—hallmarks of gradualism and interest-rate smoothing. The emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent goal and “monitoring inflation developments closely” supports expectations management while balance-sheet normalization plans and implementation via IOER/ON RRP aim for steady normalization without abrupt tightening.

Incorporating the April 2017 SLOOS:
- Banks reported tightening standards for auto loans and tighter conditions/less favorable outlook in CRE (vacancy and capitalization rate concerns), with some reports of wider loan-rate spreads and use of interest-rate floors (notably among foreign banks).
- Offsetting this somewhat, banks reported easing standards for credit card loans and a willingness to lend on consumer installment loans.

These mixed-to-slightly-tighter credit conditions temper the otherwise mildly positive macro tone from the FOMC, nudging the assessment a bit more cautious.
